dependencies: core Lean 4 only (no mathlib, no Batteries, no external imports)
gate_reuse: Checked by the existing, unmodified papers/data/lean/verify_wayfinder_axioms.py, invoked with --axioms <captured kernel output> --manifest papers/data/lean/radius-scope.json. No existing gate, test, or recorded negative was changed or relaxed to admit this file.
axiom_policy: Every declaration listed in `theorems` must appear in the `#print axioms` output of the pinned kernel run. Its reported axiom set must be a subset of `permitted_axioms` (the three core Lean assumptions). Any other axiom, and in particular `sorryAx`, fails the gate. A missing declaration fails the gate. The gate parses the kernel's printed output; it does not grep source comments.
tie_convention: A pair is CONNECTED at radius r iff d < r (strict); a tie d = r is NOT an edge. A point is ISOLATED at radius r iff r <= d, so ties fall on the off/isolated side. RadiusBounds.conn_iso_complementary pins this complementarity in the kernel.
perturbation_premise: In the Int perturbation theorems, the bound 2*e on the change of a pair distance is a PREMISE supplied by the caller. Lean does not prove that the floating-point implementation respects any such bound; that is a runtime obligation.

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.conn_iso_complementary
theorems.statement: connAt distance radius + isoAt distance radius = 1 (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: edge iff d < r (strict); isolated iff r <= d; ties are isolated, never edges

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoAt_le_one
theorems.runtime_predicate: the indicator is a 0/1 bit, never a multiplicity

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoAt_zero
theorems.runtime_counterpart: degenerate radius-0 endpoint of a radius sweep
theorems.runtime_predicate: at radius 0 no pair is an edge, so every point is isolated

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoAt_tie
theorems.runtime_counterpart: exact strict-threshold tie case in the radius sweep
theorems.runtime_predicate: at radius exactly equal to the nearest-neighbour distance the point counts as isolated

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoAt_antitone
theorems.statement: r <= s implies isoAt distance s <= isoAt distance r (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: a point that is isolated at a larger radius is isolated at every smaller radius

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoCount_nil
theorems.runtime_counterpart: empty-list base case of the isolate census
theorems.runtime_predicate: no points means no isolates at any radius

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoCount_cons
theorems.statement: isoCount (d :: ds) r = isoAt d r + isoCount ds r (Nat)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: accumulation step of the isolate census
theorems.runtime_predicate: the census sums each point's indicator exactly once

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.radius_count_antitone
theorems.statement: r <= s implies isoCount distances s <= isoCount distances r (Nat)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: I(r) isolate-count curve over a radius sweep
theorems.runtime_predicate: the isolate count is antitone in the radius: enlarging the radius never increases it

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isoCount_le_length
theorems.runtime_predicate: the isolate count never exceeds the number of points

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.isolated_perturbation
theorems.statement: r + 2*e <= d and d <= dnew + 2*e implies r <= dnew (Int)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: conditional isolate-persistence check under a bounded coordinate perturbation
theorems.runtime_predicate: a pair with integer clearance at least 2*e stays a non-edge; the bound 2*e is a supplied premise, not a proved float property

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.connected_perturbation
theorems.statement: d + 2*e < r and dnew <= d + 2*e implies dnew < r (Int)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: conditional edge-persistence check under a bounded coordinate perturbation
theorems.runtime_predicate: a strictly-interior pair stays an edge under the same premise; strictness matches the runtime d < r edge test

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.perturbation_band
theorems.statement: dnew <= d + 2*e and d <= dnew + 2*e implies -(2*e) <= dnew - d and dnew - d <= 2*e (Int)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: statement of the perturbation premise used by the two persistence theorems
theorems.runtime_predicate: the two directional premises are exactly a symmetric band on the distance change

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clampLow_ge
theorems.runtime_counterpart: lower clip of an interval to the display window
theorems.runtime_predicate: clipping never moves an endpoint below the window

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clampHigh_le
theorems.runtime_counterpart: upper clip of an interval to the display window
theorems.runtime_predicate: clipping never moves an endpoint above the window

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clipLen_nonneg
theorems.runtime_predicate: an empty overlap reports 0, never a negative extent

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clipLen_le_window
theorems.statement: lo <= hi implies clipLen lo hi a b <= hi - lo (Int)
theorems.runtime_predicate: a clipped extent never exceeds the window extent

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clipArea_nonneg
theorems.statement: 0 <= clipArea lo1 hi1 a1 b1 lo2 hi2 a2 b2 (Int)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: integer skeleton of the clipped-area diagnostic
theorems.runtime_predicate: the exact integer clipped area is non-negative

theorems.name: RadiusBounds.clipArea_le_window
theorems.statement: lo1 <= hi1 and lo2 <= hi2 implies clipArea lo1 hi1 a1 b1 lo2 hi2 a2 b2 <= (hi1 - lo1) * (hi2 - lo2) (Int)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: integer skeleton of the clipped-area diagnostic
theorems.runtime_predicate: the exact integer clipped area never exceeds the window area

runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.detail: That the runtime's floating-point chord distances on the 0.2 frame, and the canonical radius 0.095, can be reduced to the exact Nat/Int order predicates used here. No float error bound is proved by the kernel.
That a coordinate perturbation of magnitude e really induces a pair-distance change of at most 2*e in the runtime's metric and arithmetic. Supplied as a premise; checked, if at all, by runtime tests.
That the runtime builds the distance list used by I(r) with each point enumerated exactly once and with its true nearest-neighbour distance.

The runtime's clipped area and area/N ratio are RUNTIME-DERIVED floating-point quantities. Section 3 of RadiusBounds.lean is an exact integer lemma set only; it is NOT a kernel theorem about the runtime float area, and no correspondence between the two is proved.

nonclaims: No floating-point error bound, metric correspondence, chord-distance identity, or scaling law is proved; all statements are exact integer arithmetic.
The continuous clipped area and area/N used by the runtime are runtime-derived, not new kernel theorems.
No probabilistic certificate, confidence interval, significance claim, or calibration claim is proved.
No Ginzburg-Landau / Allen-Cahn dynamics, vortex classification, winding number, physical phase, or thermodynamic statement follows from these theorems.
No claim about prediction accuracy, prospective forecasting skill, ranking quality, or semantic task grading.
The canonical radius 0.095 is unchanged; nothing here admits a new score, ranking, or keep/revert/delete policy.
A displayed radius sweep remains diagnostic; these theorems do not license changing the operative metric.
A checked identity here is not evidence that the runtime diagnostic is correctly wired; see runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.

statement_pinning.pin: sha256 of the normalized Lean statement text
statement_pinning.normalization: Lean comments stripped (/- -/ nested blocks, -- line); string literals respected; statement = source text between the declaration name and the first top-level ':=' (or the first top-level match-arm '|' line for pattern proofs); whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces; proof text excluded.
statement_pinning.policy: A pin mismatch fails CI. A legitimate statement change requires a deliberate pin regeneration in the same PR, with the statement diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate pins to make CI pass without reviewing the statement diff.
